@mdink · visual and release-readiness report

Before → after.

A self-contained record of the docs redesign, runnable onboarding, package release lane, and real native editing films completed on 26 August 2026.

Implementation verified

A clearer first impression.

The original hero explained the product, but looked like a conventional developer landing page. The new direction uses Markdown source as its visual language: mono typography, structural rules, and live native proof.

Static screenshot → two real native edits

The proof now moves on iPhone and Mac.

These paired 14-second recordings run the same Markdown through the production UIKit/TextKit and AppKit/TextKit editors. Each types through its ordinary native input path, builds a task list and table, selects a deliberate typo, corrects it, and applies the public bold command.

  • Real Swift app captures—not browser recreations.
  • Real incremental edits—not pre-rendered typewriter overlays.
  • One compact iPhone/Mac switcher keeps both films legible.
  • Muted, looping, inline playback with controls and poster fallbacks.

From repository tour to runnable start.

The old guide began with build tooling, had no registry command, and used host-only variables. The new guide opens with the integration choice and gives complete Web, React, and Swift paths.

What changed.

The release surface and documentation now describe the same package boundaries.

Verification record.

Checks ran against production builds and rendered pages—not only source files.

Production buildSite, Rust/Wasm core, and all four npm packages built successfully.
Native filmsBoth high-resolution H.264 captures were verified frame by frame at 30 fps and about 14 seconds: iPhone 1080×2348 / 492 KB; Mac 1800×1080 / 599 KB.
Web suite154 tests passed; 3 intentionally skipped. Verified pages logged no warnings or errors.
Swift suite161 tests passed; 17 opt-in benchmarks skipped. The package manifest and native renderer built from a clean cache.
npm artifactsFour tarballs validated for runtime files, declarations, Wasm/CSS, README, changelog, license, public access, provenance, and resolved internal ranges.
Docs contentWeb and React install commands found; zero starter placeholders or misspelled vendor paths remained.
Responsive layout1280 px and 390 px viewports verified; the two-platform player moves from the hero’s right side to a single-column mobile stack.

Responsive proof

The hierarchy survives the small screen.

  • Headline stays readable without clipping.
  • Calls to action become full-width tap targets.
  • The iPhone/Mac player stacks below the platform list.
  • Both native tabs remain visible and tappable.
  • Document width matches the viewport.

Release boundary.

The checkout is implementation-ready; identity-bearing account settings remain external.

  • Connect the final GitHub repository and add its exact package metadata.
  • Confirm ownership of the @mdink npm scope and configure release.yml as trusted publisher.
  • Prepare the first Swift release using that owner/repository slug and attach its archive.

No package was published and no repository was created. The checked-in workflow and release guide make the remaining handoff explicit.
